subject: Chemistry
name: Theory (Core)
description: Core theory covering formulae and compounds, water analysis, iron extraction, Group I elements, organic chemistry, halogens and electrolysis, sulfur and compounds, and rate of reaction.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: A list of formulae: CaCO₃, CaO, Cl₂, CH₄, C₂H₅OH, C₂H₆, CuSO₄, H₂, H₂O, MgO, NaCl, SO₂. State which formula represents a compound that is the main constituent of natural gas.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: State which formula represents an element that is used in water treatment.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: State which formula represents an element that bleaches damp litmus paper.

parts.label: a(iv)
parts.question: State which formula represents a compound that contains an ion with a single negative charge.

parts.label: a(v)
parts.question: State which formula represents a hydrocarbon that is formed by the decomposition of vegetation.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Complete the dot-and-cross diagram to show the electron arrangement in a molecule of water (H₂O). Show outer shell electrons only. O has 6 outer electrons, each H has 1; two O-H bonds and two lone pairs.

parts.label: c
parts.question: State whether calcium oxide is a basic oxide or an acidic oxide. Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Table shows ion masses in 1000 cm³ of lake water: Ca²⁺ 0.41 mg, Cl⁻ 4.40 mg, Mg²⁺ 0.39 mg, NO₃⁻ 0.03 mg, K⁺ 0.30 mg, SiO₃²⁻ 0.02 mg, Na⁺ 2.90 mg, SO₄²⁻ 2.80 mg. State which negative ion has the lowest concentration.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Name the compound containing Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ ions.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Calculate the mass of chloride ions in 250 cm³ of lake water. (Chloride: 4.40 mg per 1000 cm³.)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Describe a test for sulfate ions.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: The structure of citric acid is shown (contains 3 COOH carboxylic acid groups, C₆H₈O₇). Deduce the number of carboxylic acid groups in one molecule of citric acid.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: The formula of citric acid is C₆H₈O₇. Complete the table to calculate Mr. C: 6×12=72, H: 8×1=8, O: 7×16=112. Find Mr.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Iron is extracted from iron ore in a blast furnace. Name an ore of iron.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Complete the chemical equation for the reduction of iron(III) oxide in the blast furnace. Fe₂O₃ + .....CO → .....Fe + 3CO₂

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: State the meaning of the term reduction.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Calcium carbonate (limestone) is added to the blast furnace and undergoes thermal decomposition. State the meaning of the term thermal decomposition.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Iron can be made into stainless steel. Give one use of stainless steel.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Describe one advantage of stainless steel compared with pure iron.

parts.label: e
parts.question: The symbol for an isotope of iron is ⁵⁷Fe (atomic number 26). Deduce the number of electrons, neutrons and protons in one atom of this isotope.

parts.label: f
parts.question: Iron is a good conductor of heat and electricity. Give two other physical properties of iron that are characteristic of all metals.

parts.label: g
parts.question: Iron rusts. Name the two substances needed for iron to rust.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Table shows Group I element properties: Li (mp 181°C, density 0.53), Na (mp 98°C, rapid bubbling, no flame), K (density 0.86, rapid bubbling, lilac flame), Rb (mp 39°C, density 1.53, very rapid bubbling, red flame), Cs (mp 29°C, density 1.88, explodes), Fr (mp 27°C). Predict the melting point of potassium and the density of francium.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Describe the observations when lithium reacts with water.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Deduce the electronic structure of sodium (atomic number 11).

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Explain why a potassium ion has a single positive charge.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Sodium reacts with water to produce aqueous sodium hydroxide and a gas which 'pops' with a lighted splint. Complete the chemical equation: 2Na + 2H₂O → .....NaOH + ..........

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Choose one value that best describes the pH of aqueous sodium hydroxide. Circle your answer.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Table shows structures of organic compounds: G (C₃H₈ propane) – alkane (given); H (C₂H₅OH ethanol); J (C₃H₆ propene). Complete the table by naming the homologous series for compounds H and J.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Draw the structure of a compound containing two carbon atoms which belongs to the same homologous series as compound H (ethanol, C₂H₅OH). Show all atoms and bonds.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Compound J (propene) is an alkene. Describe the colour change when excess compound J is added to aqueous bromine.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Compound J can be obtained by cracking petroleum fractions. State the conditions needed for cracking.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Complete this sentence about cracking using a word from the list: bitumen, hydrogen, oxygen, petroleum. The chemicals manufactured by cracking include alkanes, alkenes and .......................... .

parts.label: e
parts.question: Compound G is propane. Complete the word equation for the complete combustion of propane. propane + oxygen → ........................ + ........................

parts.label: f(i)
parts.question: Compound J (propene) can form polymers. State the meaning of the term polymer.

parts.label: f(ii)
parts.question: Nylon is also a polymer. Give one use of nylon.

parts.label: f(iii)
parts.question: Describe one pollution problem caused by non-biodegradable plastics.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Diagrams show part of the structures of potassium iodide (giant ionic lattice of K⁺ and I⁻ ions) and bromine (simple molecular, Br₂ molecules). Describe the physical properties in terms of volatility, solubility in water, and electrical conductivity when molten (liquid).

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Molten potassium iodide is electrolysed using carbon (graphite) electrodes. Name the substance produced at the positive electrode.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Complete the word equation: potassium iodide + bromine → ........................ + ........................

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.question: Explain in terms of the reactivity of the halogens why aqueous potassium chloride does not react with aqueous bromine.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Name the change of state when liquid bromine changes to solid bromine.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Use the kinetic particle theory to describe the differences between sulfur gas and solid sulfur in terms of the arrangement and separation of the particles.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Give the major use of sulfur in industry.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Sulfur dioxide is a pollutant that contributes to acid rain. State one adverse effect of sulfur dioxide on health.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Name one other oxide that contributes to acid rain.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: SO₂ reacts with water to produce sulfurous acid: SO₂ + H₂O ⇋ H₂SO₃. The reaction is reversible. Draw the symbol for a reversible reaction.

parts.label: d
parts.question: The equation is Na₂SO₃ + 3Zn → Na₂S + 3ZnO. Explain how this equation shows that zinc is oxidised.

parts.label: a
parts.question: A student investigates CaCO₃ with excess HCl: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + CO₂ + H₂O. Graph shows mass of reaction mixture vs time: mass decreases from about 200g, levelling off at about 197.5g after about 100s. Deduce the time taken for the mass to decrease by 1.0g.

parts.label: b
parts.question: The experiment was repeated using HCl of higher concentration. All other conditions stayed the same. Draw a line on the grid to show how the mass changes with time. (Describe: steeper initial slope, same final mass, reaches endpoint sooner.)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Describe the effect on the rate of reaction when: (1) carried out at a higher temperature; (2) using large pieces of CaCO₃ instead of small pieces. All other conditions stay the same.

parts.label: d
parts.question: When 0.44g of CaCO₃ is used, 100 cm³ of CO₂ is formed. Calculate the mass of CaCO₃ needed to produce 25 cm³ of CO₂.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Table shows reaction of four metals with dilute HCl: Fe (bubbles slowly), Mg (bubbles very rapidly), Ni (bubbles very slowly), Ag (no bubbles). Put the metals in order of reactivity, least reactive first.
